title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Lenses — 2022
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: State the thin lens maker's formula. Derive it for a convex lens.
questions.solution:
**Lens maker's formula:** 1/f = (μ-1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂)

Derivation: Using refraction at two spherical surfaces and applying sign convention for thin lens:
For first surface: (μ-1)/R₁ contribution
For second surface: -(μ-1)/R₂ contribution
Adding: 1/f = (μ-1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂)

Where μ = refractive index of lens material, R₁ and R₂ are radii of curvature of the two surfaces.
questions.knowledgeNote: For a double convex lens with equal radii R: 1/f = 2(μ-1)/R
questions.answer: **Thin lens maker's formula:** **1/f = (n − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂)**, where n is the refractive index of the lens material relative to the surroundings, R₁ the radius of the first (front) surface and R₂ of the second (back) surface, with radii positive for surfaces convex toward the incoming light. It gives the focal length from the *material and geometry* of the lens, independent of where the object is. **Derivation for a convex lens (two refractions in succession):** **(1) First surface:** light from a point object O at distance u refracts at the first surface (radius R₁) and would form an image I′ at distance v′: n₂/v′ − n₁/u = (n₂ − n₁)/R₁ (refraction at a single spherical surface). With n₁ = 1 (air), n₂ = n: n/v′ − 1/u = (n − 1)/R₁. **(2) Second surface:** the image I′ acts as the (virtual) object for the second surface (radius R₂); the final image I forms at v: treating the glass-to-air refraction, 1/v − n/v′ = (1 − n)/R₂ = −(n − 1)/R₂. **(3) Add the two equations:** the internal terms n/v′ cancel: 1/v − 1/u = (n − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂). **(4) Define the focal length:** for an object at infinity (u → ∞), 1/v = 1/f, so **1/f = (n − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂)**. **Deep point:** the derivation is two single-surface refractions added so the intermediate image cancels — the lens never does anything but bend light twice; the 'maker' in the name is because the formula tells the grinder what radii and glass to choose for a wanted f.
